name: 22 Watervalle
highlights:
This is a beautiful, large campsite which sprawls along a river. The sites themselves are generally very well shaded and quite big.

The campsite's highlight is obviously the waterfalls and the surrounding nature. You really should bring your hiking shoes and your swimming gear.
remember:
The hike up to see the 22 waterfalls is quite strenuous. It's a climb up a gorge rather than a walk along a valley. The hike to the first waterfall is quick and easy. This one is already quite spectacular, and you definitely shouldn't miss it if you're camping there.

From there, you immediately have to start climbing up ladders, and this is how much of this hike continues. This is not meant for younger children.

There's a short hike directly from the office which takes you to the 3rd waterfall. This is one of the bigger waterfalls and is a must-see. There's a lovely pool at the base of the waterfall, allowing you to swim under the waterfall and get a lovely water massage.
features: Electricity, Shop available, Alternative Accommodation, Swimming, Fishing, Hiking Trails

name: Kruistementvlei
highlights:
This is a very unique experience and not at all your traditional campsite. The campsite itself is rustic, off-grid, and private. You feel like you are entirely isolated and able to reconnect with nature.

Walking around on the farm (it's not particularly big) was great as you discovered all the interesting nooks and crannies. There are lots of paths to walk or jog as you criss-cross the property and discover all there is, from a forest, a clay pit and a large bench made from that clay.

We missed the monthly market (it was moved due to the weather), but the little bit of it we did catch looked wonderful. We could only imagine how much fun it would've been if it was on the farm.

The outdoor shower, heated by a donkey and open to the stars is also quite special.
remember:
The campsite is off-grid and very rustic, so there are no power points at all. You also have long-drop toilets, but they are very sanitary and cleaned often.

The road to the farm is perfectly fine for any vehicle, but the final 100m stretch of road on the farm itself is quite tight. We got through with our camping van (quite a large one), but a caravan would struggle a lot.
spots:
There are no demarcated spots. We were fortunate that we were the only people camping there and generally they do it more for a group. A larger group would be able to use the campsite.

Seeing as there are no demarcated spots, it's worthwhile checking how many other campers will be there. Anything more than 3 groups would become crowded quickly, as the space feels like it has been set up with a single group in mind.
features: Rowing, Kids Play Area, Pet Friendly, Alternative Accommodation, Swimming, Swimming Pool, Hiking Trails

name: Groot Breede
highlights:
This lovely campsite is situated next to the Breederiver. The sites are very large and have incredible shade throughout the day. Every site is right next to the river and has a private ablution. It's a relatively small campsite, so you're likely to enjoy peace and quiet. 

We really enjoyed the river. It's a fantastic family-friendly river - gentle enough not to be dangerous, deep enough to be fun, even for the adults. The pile of tubes that were available were also a great source of fun.
remember:
Like many campsites in the area, the flood from early in 2026 cause some damage here, but luckily it seems they were spared from too much damage. When we visited, they were expanding the ablutions and looked likely to add some more sites, as there's ample space to do so.

The ablutions are not on the same level as the sites, so it's a bit of a walk up the stairs to get to your ablution. Each site has access to its own bathroom, but there's also a family bathroom and communal bathroom available.
spots: 1 is closest to the bathroom, and then you move progressively further away. 10 is closest to the river entry point. Other than that they're all very much the same. Big and with ample shade.
features: Rowing, Electricity, Shop available, Private Ablutions, Swimming, Fishing, Hiking Trails

name: Kliprivier Park
highlights:
This is an older park that was closed down for some time and has recently opened up again. You can see that not all parts of it have been fully restored to functionality, but the care and friendliness of the staff is exceptional. By far the greatest highlight here was just how friendly the entire staff were throughout our stay.

Because you can see it's an older park there are big trees everywhere, providing ample shade on most of the campsites. The grass is also well looked after and the sites are very level.

We also liked the location for being just outside of Tulbagh and very central if you want to explore the area further.
remember:
They have a noise policy that allows music from 08:00 - 20:00, but require you to do this while still respecting fellow campers. There's also a pub pretty close to the campsite which we could hear quite clearly. We weren't bother too much, but you won't get the absolute peace and quiet other campsites might give you.

They don't have a shop, but they do sell ice and firewood.
spots:
There's not much to choose between the spots as they are all well covered in grass and have  ample shade. 

We had one of the spots right next to the river. It's beautiful, but the ablutions are about 50m away, which can be pretty far at night. There are several chalets on the other side of the river which could get a bit more rowdy. Asking for a spot futher down the river and closer to the secondary ablution would be quieter.

They are clearly still restoring parts of this campsite. Some of the older spots further away from the main camp look great and it's well worth enquiring about the off-grid spots.
features: Rowing, Kids Play Area, Electricity, Alternative Accommodation, Fishing, Swimming Pool

name: Ebb & Flow
highlights:
The campsite is very family-oriented with lush green grass, lots of trees for shade and beautiful nature. 

There are lots of nature-related activities in the area, from enjoying the river to hiking the surrounding mountains and finding waterfalls.

Wilderness is a great little town with a vibrant, lively culture and a spectacular sprawling beach.
remember: The camp is divided into the North and the South sides. The North side is a thin strip snaking along the river, while the South side is slightly bigger and has the offices and alternative accommodation options. The South side feels in a way like the more commercialised option, with the North feeling more rustic.
spots: We unfortunately experienced some rain and didn't get a good look around at all the campsites. We were on the North side and felt this was the nicer side.
features: Cycling, Rowing, Electricity, Alternative Accommodation, Swimming, Fishing, Hiking Trails

name: Nature's Valley Rest Camp
highlights:
You're as in the forest as possible, surrounded by trees and dense shade throughout the day. Even though there are a lot of other campsites, the trees create natural space between these sites and you never feel cramped. 

The trees are both a blessing and a curse as they can make manoeuvring with a trailer quite tricky, and a caravan a true test of skill.

You are right next to the river and there's a launching area, so canoeing or paddleboarding is highly recommended. Canoes are also available for rent. There are lots of hiking routes in the area, for all skill levels. These are an absolute must if you're visiting the area.

The small town of Nature's Valley is right around the corner and the lagoon area is quite spectacular.
remember:
There are sites with power and those without power. Those without power tend to have slightly more trees and are more suited to tented camping. Note that solar panels are rendered largely useless with the dense shade from the trees.

Most of the sites with power are a little closer to the edge of the campsite. This area is supposedly plagued by baboons a little more. The sites are however a bit bigger and easier to navigate for camp trailers.

You have to be on your guard with the baboons as they're very opportunistic. They're not aggressive or dangerous, but if you leave food lying around unattended or leave your tents open, you will have problems.
spots:
Sites work on a first come first serve basis. Spend some time wandering the sites before committing too quickly. 

We thought the following sites looked good: 
With power - 28, 30
Without power - 39, 44, 45
features: Cycling, Rowing, Electricity, Shop available, Alternative Accommodation, Swimming, Hiking Trails

name: Skilpadbessie
highlights:
This is a wonderfully secluded campsite. There are only two sites, and the owners have gone to great lengths to ensure that you feel secluded from the other site.

The site itself is beautifully kept with immaculate bathrooms. Each campsite has its own bathroom.

The fact that you're out of town, largely on your own, with no power, gives this place a magical atmosphere. There are great little touches throughout the experience that elevate this spot beyond your usual campsites.

If you're planning on going as a bigger group and taking both sites, there's a lovely communal braai area. Anyone can use this, even if you're only on one of the sites.
remember:
There is no power at the campsite, so ensure you charge your electronics up. The bathroom works with an old donkey to provide hot water and there are a few solar lights scattered throughout, but other than that you're on your own.

There's running water, but not suited for drinking, so bring enough water. There's no shade for your tent / camping van, but each site has a very nice gazebo with a picnic bench.
spots: Soutbossie. This one is quite a lot nicer than the other one. It has an amazing wood-fired hot tub while the other one does not.
features: Private Ablutions, Private Sites, Swimming Pool, Hiking Trails, 4 x 4

name: Bontebok National Park
highlights: Nature nature nature! The campsite and the facilities are in immaculate condition. There are lots of really well demarcated hiking trails and even cycling trails. There is are no dangerous animals, so you can walk, cycle and kayak all over the place. The game drives aren't great, but the Bontebokke basically live in the campsite! This is really special. If you already have a Wildcard, this is a very affordable campsite.
remember: Bring your hiking shoes! There are lots of incredible hiking trails. The picnic area "Die Stroom" is well worth a visit with lots of seating and braai facilities overlooking the river. There's no shop, so bring ice and enough firewood along.
spots:
Campsite 9 was great. It almost feels like private camping.
Sites 5 and 2 are also very good.

Note: You cannot pre-book any sites. It's on a first-come basis.
features: Cycling, Rowing, Kids Play Area, Electricity, Alternative Accommodation, Fishing, Hiking Trails, 4 x 4

name: Leeuwenboschfontein
highlights: This is an absolutely beautiful campsite with terrific shade and really good facilities. The sites are large, well demarcated and have good shade throughout the day. This is a hidden gem in the middle of nowhere. There are plenty of things to do for all ages. The closeness to nature is evidenced by the frog choir and the spectacular night sky.
remember: The nearest town is about 35 km away on a gravel road, but the shop sells all the basics.
spots:
2, 4, 13, 6
We thought 16 was the winner though!
features: Rowing, Kids Play Area, Electricity, Shop available, Alternative Accommodation, Private Sites, Fishing, Swimming Pool, Hiking Trails, 4 x 4

name: Batis & Bass
highlights: There are two large private camp sites. Both have good communal areas and they're ideal for large groups. The shade is limited, but the river is wonderful and very kids friendly.
remember: It can get quite windy next to the river, so wind screens can help. The directions to the site aren't great.
spots: We preferred Bass. It has less shade, but the communal area is better.
features: Rowing, Electricity, Pet Friendly, Private Ablutions, Swimming, Private Sites, Fishing

name: Silwerstrand
highlights: The campsite is very kids friendly and is very well kept. There are lots of options to keep the kids entertained, especially during the warmer months with a fun supertube into a pool and an amazing river. This is an absolute must for those who have boats. Kayaks can also be rented.
remember: The shop is very limited and is cash only. You can however go next door to the day visitors for a larger selection. Bring long leads as some of the powerpoints are quite far away.
spots:
We thought nr 8 is the best spot. 
2, 5, 7 and 20 are also good spots.

name: Onrus Caravan Park
highlights: This is a very well-kept campsite with great amenities. You are right next to the ocean and several sites have a sea view. You also have easy access to the ocean at Davy's Pool. Onrus is also a an area with lots of things to do.
remember: If you have some form of wind screens, this is quite useful as the ocean breeze can be troublesome at some sites.
spots:
68, 67, 56, 30, 26, 16 (for a tent)
38 in Summer
175 would also be nice for multiple smaller tensts
features: Kids Play Area, Electricity, Shop available, Swimming, Fishing, Restaurant

name: Melkhout Guest Farm
highlights: Each site has its own large, covered deck overlooking the river. The deck doesn't only have great views, it provides ample shade and is well equipped. At the back of the deck, is your private ablution, lots of plugs and a hot & cold water sink to for washing up. There's also a spacious picnic table in the middle of the deck. This truly is spectacular and quite unique! The river itself is of course great, and the boathouse houses 4 large kayaks which you can take out on the river free of charge.
remember: The river is great, but not kid-friendly for swimming. It gets very deep, very quickly.
spots:
There are only 5 sites, and you really can't go wrong with any of them. 
Number 4 is slightly bigger than the rest (you would easily have enough space for at least 3 camping trailers/tents, etc. and still have a space to pass a ball around), but doesn't have much shade. 
Number 5 is probably the smallest (still more than big enough for 2 camping trailers), but has the best shade and is the most private. This would be our top pick.

name: De Hoop Campsite
highlights: It's an incredibly beautiful reserve with lots of nature activities. There are no dangerous animals in the reserve, which means you can hike or bike anywhere and experience nature up close and personal.
remember: A long lead (20m) is essential. Bicycles are a must, but can also be rented. Bring your hiking shoes!
spots:
No 9 is a PRIME spot. It's totally covered and very close to the ablution.
No 5 and 7 are also good alternate options.
The views at 2 & 3 are great, but you are very exposed to the elements. We struggled a lot with wind.
features: Cycling, Kids Play Area, Electricity, Shop available, Swimming Pool, Restaurant, Hiking Trails, Alternative Accommodation

name: Franschhoek Camping
highlights: This unique campsite is ideal for a private getaway. You're still close enough to an endless supply of activities in Franschhoek, but it feels very relaxed and away from it all. The sites are very well maintained and create a sense of privacy with natural barriers between all the sites. Most sites are equipped with your own pergola and have access to a private bathroom. The campsite's rules add to this relaxing atmosphere as they do not allow any children under 12.
remember: One of the key rules to keep in mind is that you are not allowed to camp in tents nor are you allowed to use any ground covers. A private Kolkol (hot tub) can be arranged prior to your visit.
spots:
Number 10 is definitely the prime spot. This one is slightly bigger than the rest, a bit more private and has a fantastic private bathroom.
Number 6 and Number 3 are also good spots.
features: Electricity, Shop available, Private Ablutions, Swimming Pool, Alternative Accommodation

name: Breede Otter
highlights: This is a very large campsite, ideal for big groups. You can even use the spacious lapa by prior arrangement to use for bigger groups. During our visit, the river was very child-friendly, and during the warmer months, this site is all about the river. It's a very well-maintained campsite with immaculately clean bathrooms.
remember: Be sure to bring your own flotation devices. Because of the floods of 2024 and 2023, the campsite lost a lot of shade, so bringing some extra shade options is recommended.
spots:
37A and 37B (in Kolgans) are very good. They're close to the river and have some decent shade.
The Boskamp sites, especially 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8 are really nice with good shade, by the river, but they are without electricity.
features: Kids Play Area, Electricity, Pet Friendly, Shop available, Swimming, Fishing, Hiking Trails

name: Lylius

remember: No cellphone reception. Bring your hiking boots!
spots: Pear, Mango

highlights: Big campsites in die beautiful Slanghoek Vallei.

name: Schoongezicht

remember: Pack in your walking shoes and enjoy exploring the area.

name: Môreson
highlights:
One of the best aspects of Môreson is the privacy. Each campsite has its own ablution and a fence has been built between the different campsites. 
Every campsite has full shade all day long.
remember: The campsites have no grass covering, one of the trade-offs for the great shade you get.
spots: The spots are all well shaded and you can't really go wrong with any of them.

name: Skurwekop
highlights: At Skurwekop you can either camp on the river or a few campsites in.  All river campsites are fenced, which makes it safe for kids.  There are also pull carts for the little ones to make a ride around the site easier and way more fun.  Kayaks can be rented from the shop.
remember: The shop opens twice a day and for a limited time, make sure you are there if you need anything.

name: Kam'Bati

remember: Bring lots of sunblock for the kids as the water activities keeps them busy the whole day.

highlights:
Lovely Campsite in a National Park.  Very Family friendly with lots of families camping.  The game drives are always exciting with all the elephants and other game to view.
.

name: Vloedbos
highlights: With Supertubes, pools, playpaks and put-put there is a lot to keep the family busy.
features: Kids Play Area, Electricity, Shop available, Swimming, Fishing, Swimming Pool, Restaurant, Alternative Accommodation

name: Dwarsberg Trout Hideaway
highlights: Private, big camp sites for groups. Incredible nature surrounds. This is a very tranquil and serene experience for groups.
remember: Remember your fishing rod as there is really good fishing here (the name says it all) on a catch-and-release basis.

name: Rivierplaas
highlights: Situated on the banks of the Breede River they offer big stretched out lawns and child-friendly play areas. Other features include the relatively deep swimming area and foefie slide (flying fox) into the river. There are also inner tubes, canoes and rafts available for all to use.
remember: Pack some floaties and fishing rods as there is a great river to enjoy.

name: Doornlaagte
highlights: This campsite is all about water! Facilities include a dam, kids swimming pool with slides, 3 additional swimming pools. Adults-only bar area (with pool).  This is truly a campsite to keep everyone entertained.
remember: The shop, restaurant and bar is CASH ONLY.  Also remember a fishing rod. The kayaks and other boats operate on a first-come, so you if snooze, you loose. Just remember to return them once you're done.
spots: Eiland 4,5 en 6

name: Guano Caves
highlights: With five amazing swimming pools, a petting zoo, bar, restaurant and two supertubes on the site - you are sure to have a good time.  There is even a tractor ride to a nearby cave.
remember: Remember bicycles for kids as the entertainment area is a little walk away from the campsites. Also bring lots of cash for the restaurant.

name: Stille Waters
